## Dieses Dokument

- Titel: Brief von Stefan Zweig an Hannah Altmann [2. Juni 1941], SZ-AAL/B1.136
- Signatur: SZ-AAL/B1.136
- Datum: 2.6.1941
- Objekttyp: Brief
- Umfang: 5 Scans

pages.transcription:
Hotel Wyndham 42 West 58 Street
2. June 1941
Dear Hannah we have been for one day on Atlantic
City to discuss different matters and to {get} also an im-
pression if such a place would do for the coming months
of heat. It was very pleasant now but {it will} be unpleasant
when the great crowds begin to come; so we have to look
for another place; it is not easy for old fashioned people without car.
About Eva, you will have the best news, she feels perfectly
at home {in Croton} and I shall not forget your wish that she
shall learn French during the holidays. I had two long
and very friendly letters from our friend Eize but there is
something in it which does not please me; he has since
a year not notified a single precise thing and I see
that the drawing from which you gave me news he has
afterwards sold to somebody other. I can well understand
his situation; it seems that he cannot resist the tempta-
tion if some new friends come now who were not so inter-
ested in art as myself and have discovered her inclination
but now, he forgets his old friends and also the promise he
gave to them. If he would have written straightaway: I
could not do anything this whole year for you I would
have been clear. But I cannot get rid of the idea that
he whenever a better offer comes for the same things
he reserved months and months ago for me he gives
them away with profits and forgets what {he has let him down?} Perhaps I
am wrong but there is something evasive in his letters
and I wonder if he has given {you} clear information;
pages.notes: Handschriftlicher Brief auf Hotelpapier. Tinte violett. Die Zeile 'he has let him down?' ist eine Einfügung über der Zeile.
Rückseite des ersten Blattes, durchscheinender Text der Vorderseite sichtbar. Leer.

pages.transcription:
The situation in the book market is not more the same than
a year ago and that is why I tried to reserve me in
time the material for my work. I did not write to him
myself because {it may} be a mere suspicion
of my part and as I know how hard he works, how diffi-
cult his life must be; perhaps you can make it out and
act without to let him feel that I begin to feel a bit dis-
appointed. I want to believe always the best of my
friends as long as I have no absolute proof of the
contrary. Wednesday we have our great 'spring cleaning'
- I have invited all those people I had to see to our
cocktail. It is impossible to make visits here {individually} 
by it takes too much time and the distances are too
great.
You never wrote me dear Hannah if there any
books or letters of interest came all this year long; I
do not want of course the whole list {and busy that} if anything
of personal interest would arrive you will let me
know it; altogether our correspondence is very small
now during that all writers are already {have} arrived here
I hope you will {have} with brillant teeth a brillant
summer in Bath and enjoy after Manfrets examina-
tion the well merited rest. Lotte is much better, she has
lost a litte weight and I will do my best to let her
regain all his ounces; if we only could sit some-
where quitely and be out of this Hotel and hometic
life! Yours faithful
Stefan
pages.notes: Handschriftlicher Brief, Fortsetzung auf zweitem Blatt. Tinte violett.
Rückseite des zweiten Blattes, durchscheinender Text der Vorderseite sichtbar. Leer.

result.confidence_notes: Der Text ist sehr gut lesbar, trotz einiger Korrekturen und Einfügungen durch den Autor. Die Handschrift ist charakteristisch für Stefan Zweig.
